name: Wang Wan
bio: Wang Wan was a T’ang poet who took his degree in AD 712, according to the chronology of poets in The Jade Mountain.
The poem here is Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu’s version in The Jade Mountain (1929), given with the poet’s name as spelled here.

poems.title: A Mooring Under North Fort Hill
poems.author: Wang Wan
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Under blue mountains we wound our way,
My boat and I, along green water;
Until the banks at low tide widened,
With no wind stirring my lone sail.
. . . Night now yields to a sea of sun,
And the old year melts in freshets.
At last I can send my messengers —
Wildgeese, homing to Lo-yang.

poems.title: 次北固山下 (Ci bei gu shan xia)
poems.author: Wang Wan
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
客路青山外，行舟綠水前。
潮平兩岸闊，風正一帆懸。
海日生殘夜，江春入舊年。
鄉書何處達？歸雁洛陽邊。
